subject: health
unitTitle: Staying Safe at Home, Outside, and Online
title: Application or project: water safety
essentialQuestion: How do I spot a hazard early and choose the safest next step?
materials: paper or a printed checklist for a home safety walk
a properly fitted helmet if wheels are discussed
keyPoints: Never swim alone, and only swim where an adult is watching.
Open water is different from a pool: cold, currents, and hidden depth make it far less predictable.
If someone is in trouble in water, do not go in after them — shout for an adult, and reach or throw something that floats.
Wear a life jacket on boats and in open water, whatever your swimming ability.
privacySafeScenario: A friend has waded out too far in a lake and is struggling. You are a strong swimmer. What do you actually do first?
studentTask: The learner applies what they learned about water safety to a new fictional situation and records the choice plus the reason behind it.
knowledgeCheck: Show one part of your project that uses water safety and say why you made that choice.
completionCriteria: The learner completes the central task about water safety.
The learner gives a reason, an example, or a documented process rather than an unsupported answer.
The learner checks or revises the work and can name one next step.
adaptationChoices: A safety walk may be done by an adult with the learner directing from a seated position, by spoken description with no photographs taken, or entirely through a floor-plan drawing. No learner is required to reach, lift, or test any hazard.
extensionChallenge: Apply what you learned about water safety under a new constraint, compare two reasonable approaches, or teach the idea to a family member with an original fictional example.
accessibilitySupports: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Allow typed, handwritten, spoken, signed, drawn, or pointed responses; the response mode is never the standard being assessed.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, movement-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for any media.
Preserve the learning target while adjusting quantity, pacing, representation, or response mode.
trustedAdultNote: Direct urgent safety, health, or mental-health concerns to a trusted adult or qualified professional; this course is not diagnosis, therapy, or treatment.

optionalReflection.prompt: With a guardian, walk the home fire escape route and agree the outside meeting place. This is optional. No purchase, account creation, photograph, measurement, or private disclosure is required.

neverRequires: This task never requires body weight, height, BMI, or body-fat percentage.
This task never requires calorie counting or a diet or weight-loss goal.
This task never requires disclosing private medical history, a diagnosis, or sexual history.
This task never requires a photograph, video, or voice recording of the learner as proof.
This task never requires a public performance or an audience.
